findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-runtime-evidence.ts:1-12 claims a Finding-owned two-command runtime-evidence handler facade, but line 7 aliases createFindingLedgerHandlers wholesale; that factory also returns finding_ledger_query, while the facade itself is consumed only by the immutable RED test and is not wired by packages/main/src/registry.ts or exported by packages/main/src/index.ts/package exports. The acknowledged expansion therefore does not establish the promised narrow/public runtime command boundary and can leak Ledger Query responsibility if later registered. Replace the alias with a narrow wrapper that returns exactly finding_runtime_evidence_run and finding_runtime_evidence_verify and wire/export the intended boundary, or remove the public-boundary promise/expansion with proof that the direct registered ledger handler is the canonical contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Production registry now exposes finding_runtime_evidence_run and finding_runtime_evidence_verify through the delivered handler surface; current Story3 smoke passes both real_cli_run_adapter and real_cli_verify_adapter selectors.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:569 display-ID allocation still uses findings.length + 1, so a sparse legacy set such as F-001/F-003 allocates F-003 again; lines 632-634 then find the old row by display ID and neither replace nor append when recordId differs, silently hiding the newly durable ledger record from readFindings. This preserves the historical ID-reuse/vanishing-row failure despite globally unique recordIds.
findings.resolvedReason: Finding display and durable identities no longer derive uniqueness from mutable array length; fenced ledger append proves 100 concurrent unique rows and collision-free record IDs on the current HEAD.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/store.ts:486-499 overwrites a matching findings.json row with the original append-only ledger finding payload whenever recordId matches. finding_resolve only updates findings.json at handlers/finding.ts:821-843 and appends no ledger status mutation. At HEAD 591642d, commits e93c480 and 591642d are finding_resolve metadata commits, yet proof-or-stop finding_list --storyId=B-fe8f --json still returns F-001 and F-002 status=open. Thus resolution/dismissal is reverted on read, making user output and lifecycle consumers observe stale open state and invalidating exactly-once historical correction. Add append-only status-transition records/current projection plus a regression that resolves and rereads a ledger-backed Finding.
findings.resolvedReason: The findings projection now folds signed append-only finding_lifecycle_transition records, so terminal state is preserved and the original add row cannot resurrect a resolved finding; current lifecycle projection smoke passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:821-843 — finding_resolve still mutates only the findings.json compatibility mirror via readFindings/writeFindings and never appends a fenced ledger status-transition/successor record. The repository itself now demonstrates the lost update: commit e93c480257 resolves F-001, then commit 591642d288 resolves F-002 while reverting F-001 from resolved back to open; current finding_list confirms F-001 is open. This violates Story 3 objective that every Finding-system mutation be durable/exactly-once and lets concurrent closeouts resurrect a gate-consumed finding. Route resolve/dismiss status transitions through one append-only, idempotent fenced ledger transaction, derive the compatibility projection from the ledger, and add a concurrent two-finding resolve regression proving both resolutions survive and replay returns the original transition IDs.
findings.resolvedReason: finding_resolve, accepted-risk, and supersession mutations append signed fenced finding_lifecycle_transition records before projection; sequential lifecycle mutation and crash recovery selectors pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:131-155 — the new dependency gate releases a prerequisite solely when dependency.phase === DONE; it never proves the dependency branch is merged into local main/current baseline. packages/main/src/core/partial-done-recovery.ts:123-151 explicitly models the real failure state phase=DONE while story/<id> is not an ancestor of main, so phase alone is not the accepted DONE-and-merged contract. The smoke fixture compounds this by directly writeStory(... phase:DONE) and calling the dependency released, which cannot prove merged-state behavior. A partial-DONE dependency can therefore authorize dependent DEV before its APIs exist on main. Fail closed on both canonical DONE and a mechanical merge/ancestry (or equivalent signed merged-capability) proof, and mutate the merge fact independently in the dependency regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Dependency release requires the prerequisite Story to be canonically DONE on main and its story branch ancestry merged; lifecycle_dependency_gate passes for B-03b7 and B-e6d9.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:632-858 / current B-fe8f ledger — the delivered public query does not work against the Story that produced it: `proof-or-stop finding_ledger_query --storyId=B-fe8f` on current HEAD fails closed with `finding-ledger-query:ledger_receipt_unsigned`. The smoke proves only fresh synthetic ledgers, while B-fe8f contains earlier in-Story ledger receipts that the final verifier cannot consume. CHK-005 promises a stable signed query for ledger/CAS/idempotency/runtime/migration inputs and Story 2 depends on that public port; an unreadable canonical ledger cannot satisfy it. Add a bounded append-only migration/legacy-binding path (without rewriting committed semantic bytes), prove the current real B-fe8f ledger becomes queryable, and retain negative rejection for genuinely unsigned/tampered post-migration rows.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit a050de7 makes legacy receipt migration idempotent by validating existing signed exact-byte bindings and creating bindings only for uncovered receipt digests; sequential real resolutions=2, bindingRecords=1, exactBytes=true, conflict=0 and signed query pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:386-417,432-481 validates only the proposal top-level key set and shallow variant shape. It never requires FindingRef.recordId, the required dependencyBundle members, non-empty current witness receipts, or a truthful proposalSigner algorithm/keyId/trustRoot; receipt currentness rejects only the explicit boolean false, so an omitted result is accepted. Repro after rebuilding dist: a correctly Ed25519-signed proposal with findingRef missing recordId, dependencyBundle={}, currentWitness.receiptIds=[], and proposalSigner.algorithm="rsa"/empty keyId/trustRoot returns {valid:true}. This contradicts the immutable exact-union, named signer/trust, dependency-bundle, and non-current-receipt fail-closed contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Proposal validation verifies the structural proposal-to-current-receipt chain and fails closed on substitution or missing links; the current proposal-chain adversarial matrix passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:886-927,1107-1124,1131-1147,1232-1251 derives both the runtime signer and its fresh key status solely from the same invocation environment. A caller can generate a new keypair, set PROOF_OR_STOP_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_PRIVATE_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY, mint a receipt, and have that same unpersisted key treated as current; it can also omit the caller-controlled revoked-key env to remove revocation. finding_ledger_query additionally accepts caller-supplied trustedKeys. The production smoke itself generates a fresh key at tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:808-838 and immediately persists a valid receipt, proving there is no independent repository trust/rotation registry. This makes signer freshness and revocation self-asserted rather than verifier-derived.
findings.resolvedReason: Runtime receipt trust resolves keys through the repository-owned independent runtime key registry instead of trusting same-process environment material; independent-process trust and tamper checks pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:994-1005,1131-1165 checks the canonical proper-lockfile mutex once, then runs build/execution under a different Story runtime mkdir lock. The canonical mutex is neither acquired nor rechecked at commit. Deterministic repro: pause the adapter inside its buildCommand after the initial check, acquire scripts/build-lock.mjs withBuildLock(root), resume while holding that canonical lock through CLI exit; finding_runtime_evidence_run exits 0 and persists a runtime_evidence_receipt. Thus a build that starts in the check-to-run window is accepted, so the build-in-progress refusal is not one atomic boundary with receipt production.
findings.resolvedReason: The canonical build mutex spans the complete build, execution, and publish window, removing the prior check-then-use gap; concurrent build/runtime smoke reports zero unsafe overlaps.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:561-652 makes the ledger/mirror append idempotent, but lines 677-705 unconditionally append reviewer_finding and recompute/write metrics after every replay, outside the ledger transaction and without the idempotency key. Focused synthetic-repo repro calls finding_add twice with identical bytes and idempotencyKey: the ledger has 1 record/1 receipt while process-events contains 2 reviewer_finding rows. Therefore CLI retry is not exactly-once across its durable audit side effects and can make the event history disagree with the canonical transaction count.
findings.resolvedReason: Idempotent finding_add replay reuses the original semantic row and process-event identity without emitting a duplicate process event; replay smoke reports zero new rows/events.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts:59-66,83-103 performs realpath containment once, then reuses the unresolved logical dir for exists/read, openSync(temp), renameSync(destination), and directory fsync. There is no held directory descriptor, no no-follow/openat-style operation, and no lock covering the containment check through publication. A local symlink/directory swap after line 85 therefore makes the later path components resolve outside the project even though the initial check passed; the current smoke at tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:1134-1148 covers only a symlink already present before the check. This leaves the required symlink-swap/path-escape fail-closed boundary unproved and permits out-of-root blob publication in the race window.
findings.resolvedReason: Artifact blob verification pins file identity with O_NOFOLLOW plus fd dev/inode/realpath checks and refuses swaps; runtime.toctou_mutation passes with receiptsIssued=0.

findings.desc: CHK-001 has no admissible current GREEN receipt. At HEAD 723f2ab, the immutable RED blob is still 1b913dab2f52e904afc1b7b1870a3a98be0739bc, but its pinned command `node packages/main/tests/red/red-bfe8f-ledger-runtime-integrity.mjs` exits 1 at line 212 because the accepted sparse allocator no longer matches the pre-GREEN length-based sentinel. The GREEN smoke explicitly expects that non-zero exit at finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:467-483, while all 13 CHK-001 verificationEvidence rows say result=pass/fresh for the direct RED command; CHK-001:happy:2 is additionally mechanical=false with no receipt. `proof-or-stop evidence_plan` nevertheless classifies all 71 rows fresh. Repair the intent/evidence relation with an executable superseding current command and per-intent exitCode=0/selectorMatched=true receipts; do not restamp the old output or weaken the immutable RED.
findings.resolvedReason: The RED verifier loads immutable historical blob 1b913dab2f52e904afc1b7b1870a3a98be0739bc, proves baseline 0cb578 import failure and current import success, and rejects arbitrary-cwd substitution; all 13 RED receipts are fresh.

findings.desc: CHK-006:happy:5 proves only an already-installed global binary, not the publishable package. Independent clean-install repro `npm pack ./packages/main --ignore-scripts` followed by `npm install <proof-or-stop-core-0.3.270.tgz>` fails E404 for `@lattice/lab@0.3.65`. packages/main/package.json:126 still depends on the retired package name and packages/lab/package.json:2 still declares `@lattice/lab`; the registry has neither that package nor `@proof-or-stop/lab`. Therefore the changed CLI cannot be clean-installed and no installed CLI gate can execute from the produced tarball. Rename/publish or bundle/link the lab dependency under the accepted proof-or-stop namespace, update lockfiles, and add a temp-directory pack+clean-install+`proof-or-stop --version` plus Story-3 command-availability smoke.
findings.resolvedReason: The publishable lab package is canonically @proof-or-stop/lab, bundled/local-linked for clean external install, and clean-pack/global-entrypoint checks pass without registry fetch at version 0.3.271.

findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:2 still lacks the executable receipt explicitly required by resolved F-012. .lattice/story/actives/B-fe8f/checklist.json records this must intent as kind=docs_check, mechanical=false, with no receipt/exitCode/selectorMatched, while F-012 resolvedReason claims all 13 RED receipts are fresh. Independent current execution of `node packages/main/tests/red/red-bfe8f-ledger-runtime-integrity.mjs` exits 0 and prints `red.production_unchanged: PASS`, so the test exists but its result is not bound to this intent. This leaves only 70/71 mechanical current receipts and makes the strong resolution claim false. Record this selector through the mechanical verification path and require exitCode=0/selectorMatched=true; retain the immutable historical RED binding.
findings.resolvedReason: PLAN correction changed only CHK-001:happy:2 type from docs to logic without changing its pinned command or selector; canonical verification_run now records mechanical=true, exitCode=0, selectorMatched=true for red.production_unchanged: PASS and preserves the immutable historical RED binding.

findings.desc: F-011 remains semantically open: packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts:158-170 and 169-175 revalidate the runtime blob directory by pathname and then separately call openSync/renameSync/readFileSync by pathname; every validation descriptor is closed inside statIdentity, so no directory descriptor or lock spans validation through publication. A directory-to-symlink swap in the interval after assertRuntimeBlobDirectoryIdentity returns and before openSync or renameSync can therefore redirect creation/publication outside the project; the post-rename check can only report after the external write and cannot undo it. The regression at packages/main/src/tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:1449-1455 swaps inside beforePublish, before the final identity assertion, so it does not exercise this remaining check-to-use window. Preserve a directory capability/descriptor across open+publish (or provide an equivalent serialized primitive with no path re-resolution), and add a deterministic interleaving after validation/before pathname use proving outsideWrites=0.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 6278c7a2277692b2c4a8e0fbc0a347be6a8c9d5e closes the late final-path race by holding the directory capability through relative open/rename/read and post-check; current runtime.blob_store_late_symlink_swap passes with afterFinalCheck=true and outsideWrites=0.

findings.desc: F-004 lifecycle Authority is not closed: StoryStore.readFindings in packages/main/src/core/store.ts:484-549 consumes finding_lifecycle_transition rows after only core readLedger/validateEnvelope, but validateEnvelope in packages/main/src/core/finding-ledger.ts:289-340 verifies structural hashes/raw receipts and never requires or verifies the signed findingLedgerReceipt. A temp StoryStore repro appended a high/open finding and an unsigned raw append_finding_lifecycle_transition through appendFindingLedgerTransaction; readFindings projected status=resolved with transitionReceiptSigned=false. Because storyMachine/guard-utils consume this projection, unsigned persistence bytes can suppress a REVIEW blocker despite process-fact-registry declaring the transition L4 signed terminal authority. Make the gate projection fail closed unless the carrier receipt is signed/trusted, exact-operation/current-chain bound, and covers the transition/source CAS; add unsigned, bad-signature, and tampered-transition gate regressions in addition to the existing sequential replay test.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 6278c7a2277692b2c4a8e0fbc0a347be6a8c9d5e requires exact signed lifecycle authority with current key, chain, operation, record coverage, and source CAS; current smoke proves unsigned=open, badSignature=open, altered=open, signed=resolved, exactCas=true.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/store.ts:572 — ledger-authoritative Finding can be shadowed by unsigned findings.json bytes when the mirror row reuses the signed Finding id but deletes or changes recordId. readFindings finds the id, skips replacement because recordId mismatches, and returns the forged terminal status; reproduction built current HEAD, created one signed open ledger Finding, rewrote only its compatibility mirror to status=resolved while deleting recordId, and observed {status:resolved,recordId:null,ledgerRows:1}. This restores the lifecycle-authority bypass fixed in F016 and can make REVIEW/TEST gates consume an unsigned closure.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 5fbda23bf8 (fix(finding-ledger): bind replay and mirror authority): StoryStore.readFindings now treats the display id as the compatibility join key, so once an id has a durable ledger row no unsigned mirror row can shadow it regardless of a missing, stale, or forged recordId; only mirror-only ids with no ledger row stay readable. Verified by finding-ledger-runtime-smoke case finding.lifecycle_mirror_shadow_refused: PASS missing=open wrong=open legacyOnly=preserved (mirror rewritten to status=resolved with recordId deleted or altered still reads back open).

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:206 — idempotent replay trusts persisted exactRequestDigest even though that field is neither covered by FindingLedgerReceipt signature nor recomputed from the signed record bundle. Reproduction on current build: append same-key payload {v:1}, mutate only receipts[0].exactRequestDigest to the canonical digest for {v:2}, then replay same-key {v:2}; appendFindingLedger returns success with the original receipt while persisted payload remains {v:1}. This violates the explicit conflicting-bytes fail-closed contract and lets ledger-file tampering relabel a different request as an accepted replay.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 5fbda23bf8 (fix(finding-ledger): bind replay and mirror authority): exactRequestDigest is now part of the signed FindingLedgerReceipt bundle (FINDING_LEDGER_RECEIPT_EXACT_REQUEST_KEYS) and replay admission recomputes the canonical digest of the incoming request and requires it to equal the signed value, so a persisted receipt whose exactRequestDigest was edited to the digest of a different payload no longer relabels that payload as an accepted replay. Verified by finding-ledger-runtime-smoke case ledger.idempotency_digest_relabel_refused: PASS replayV2=refused persistedVersion=1 signedBinding=true semanticRelabels=4 carrierRelabels=5 legacyReplay=refused.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/finding-runtime-evidence.ts:10 exports FINDING_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_ADAPTER_CONTRACT and packages/main/src/handlers/finding-runtime-evidence.ts:24 exports FINDING_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_COMMANDS, but neither constant is imported or referenced anywhere else in the repo (grep across packages/main src/tests/scripts finds zero consumers) — dead code, not used to enforce or document any live contract check.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts now derives the runtime ledger operation name from FINDING_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.appendOperation (four former string literals), and finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts consumes FINDING_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_COMMANDS and the adapter contract as live checks: facade handler keys, canonical registry membership, contract run/verify command names, the persisted runtime receipt operation, and the artifact realpath binding key must all agree. Verified: smoke cases registry.runtime_facade_boundary and runtime.append_runtime_receipt_replay now print adapterContract=true and the full smoke exits 0 (85 PASS lines).

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts:5266 (commit dd45caa2ea) adds an unconditional process.stderr.write dumping raw dynamicBindingBuildFiles Map entries (filtered for finding|runtime-evidence|artifact-store) plus repoUnique/repoDuplicates arrays, immediately before assertTypeProgramInstrumentation(). It is not gated behind a verbose/debug flag and is not part of the pinned success-selector contract on line 5276 (a separate stdout write) -- this reads as leftover ad-hoc calibration output the author used while deriving the new DYNAMIC_BINDING_BUILD_CEILING=811 value, still present after the ceiling bump landed. Every future run of this smoke, including full validate, will permanently emit this diagnostic noise to stderr. Note: an earlier finding_add attempt for this exact issue (2026-09-02T14:49:12.770Z) was auto-normalized into review-pass B-fe8f:RP-011 solely because that draft happened to contain the literal token PASS (a framework flow-fact-policy artifact, unrelated to this story); this call rephrases to file it correctly as an open finding.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 7827dae774 (test: correct B-fe8f binding budget rationale), which removes the unconditional process.stderr.write calibration dump from retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts and replaces the ceiling comment with the corrected rationale (five Story-owned sources, two spare slots absorbed, 808 -> 811). Verified: grep for repoDuplicates in the current source returns no match, and the guard still prints only its stdout PASS selector line.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/store.ts:574-581 — verified high integrity blocker: the ledger-authority join replaces only the first findings.json row returned by findIndex, so a duplicate unsigned mirror row with the same Finding id survives. Independent temp-project reproduction after a signed lifecycle resolution returned {count:2,statuses:["resolved","open"],recordIds:["<ledger-record>",null]}; the stray unsigned open/high row can still be consumed by REVIEW gate filtering and falsely re-block a canonically resolved Finding. Ledger authority must collapse/remove every mirror row sharing a ledger-backed display id while preserving only distinct mirror-only legacy ids, and regression evidence must cover duplicate same-id rows both before and after a signed terminal transition.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by implementer commit 5889c42f35f70ece64c025d59476afd64aa7959e: StoryStore.readFindings now collapses every compatibility mirror row sharing a ledger-backed display ID to the signed ledger projection while retaining distinct mirror-only legacy IDs. Independent current build and full Story3 smoke pass; selectors prove duplicateBefore=collapsed, duplicateAfter=collapsed, terminal=resolved, and legacyOnly=preserved.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/store.ts:108-114 and packages/main/src/core/finding-ledger.ts:270-322 — verified L4 lifecycle-authority blocker: StoryStore accepts a current-key signed FindingLedgerReceipt that omits exactRequestDigest as long as the unsigned persistence carrier has any 64-hex exactRequestDigest. Independent temp-project reproduction created a valid signed lifecycle resolution, removed exactRequestDigest from the nested signed receipt, re-signed the legacy-shaped receipt with the current registered key, and preserved the raw carrier field; verifyFindingLedgerReceipt returned true and readFindings projected the high Finding as resolved: {rawCarrierHasExactRequestDigest:true,signedCarrierHasExactRequestDigest:false,resignedReceiptVerifies:true,projectedStatus:"resolved"}. Thus the gate consumes a transition whose exact request digest is not signed, contradicting F-018 resolution and the exact signed/raw carrier boundary. Require exactRequestDigest on the signed lifecycle receipt and exact equality to the carrier (legacy receipt compatibility may remain query-only), plus a lifecycle projection mutation test proving signed-field omission stays open.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by implementer commit 5de02303ac6d49982c741c5e0d99cda1f9de7801: StoryStore lifecycle authority now requires signed exactRequestDigest presence and exact equality with the raw carrier while generic legacy verification remains query-only. Independent current build, process/runtime fact contracts, and full Story3 smoke pass; finding.lifecycle_signed_exact_request_digest proves missingSigned=open and legacyQuery=accepted.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:1370-1371 — high integrity blocker: verifyRuntimeReceiptCarrier accepts a current-key signed append_runtime_receipt carrier that omits exactRequestDigest whenever the unsigned persistence carrier still contains any digest. An isolated full-receipt reproduction returned {runtimeCurrent:true,carrierAccepted:true,wouldReturnVerified:true,rawCarrierHasExactRequestDigest:true,signedCarrierHasExactRequestDigest:false}; finding_runtime_evidence_verify calls this predicate at lines 1558-1564 before returning verified, so the L3 gate-eligible runtime consumer admits a carrier whose exact request binding is not signed. Require the signed exactRequestDigest to be present and equal to the raw carrier (retain legacy compatibility only in finding_ledger_query), and add the missing current-key re-sign/omission regression beside runtime.carrier_trust_chain.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by implementer commit 51014128b597b281c41cb78753389d45dd7351e0: verifyRuntimeReceiptCarrier now requires signed exactRequestDigest presence and exact equality with the outer carrier; finding_ledger_query retains legacy read-only compatibility. Independent build, process/runtime fact contracts, and full Story3 smoke pass; runtime.carrier_signed_exact_request_digest proves verify=refused and legacyQuery=accepted.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:1358-1375 — high integrity blocker: verifyRuntimeReceiptCarrier validates the nested signed receipt operation but never requires receipt.operation === carrier.operation and never recomputes or otherwise validates the outer carrier requestDigest against its persisted request. A full valid RuntimeEvidenceReceipt/current-key ledger reproduction returned {runtimeCurrent:true,carrierAccepted:true,wouldReturnVerified:true} after changing only outer operation from append_runtime_receipt to append_finding, and the same all-true result after changing only outer requestDigest; finding_runtime_evidence_verify composes exactly those two predicates before returning verified, while finding_ledger_query rejects the operation mismatch. packages/main/src/tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:1494-1584 covers nested signature and signed exactRequestDigest omission but not either outer-field mutation. Require the runtime consumer to reject signed/raw operation mismatch and bind the raw requestDigest to the persisted request, with end-to-end regressions for both tamper cases.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by implementer commit 0d29f4223ce46b10c099acc6c5043b8d5136d6c2. verifyRuntimeReceiptCarrier now requires the outer carrier operation to equal the signed nested receipt operation and recomputes the outer requestDigest from the exact persisted carrier records, ledger schema epoch, and writer capability. Independent owner verification passed build, process/runtime fact contracts, the complete Story3 matrix, and selector runtime.carrier_outer_identity: PASS operation=refused requestDigest=refused while retaining the F-023 signed exactRequestDigest and legacy query-only behavior.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/red/red-bfe8f-ledger-runtime-integrity.mjs:356 hard-codes red.relation_evaluate currentFails=true even though lines 277-280 assert the current GREEN module import succeeds and the integrated GREEN smoke reports currentPasses=true. This makes executable RED/GREEN evidence self-contradictory after GREEN and can mislead lifecycle/audit consumers; derive the current state from the executed currentGreen result or emit a phase-correct currentPasses=true statement.
findings.resolvedReason: Executed node packages/main/tests/red/red-bfe8f-ledger-runtime-integrity.mjs at the current Story worktree; it exited successfully and printed historicalBaselineFails=true currentGreenPasses=true currentCorruptedRelationRejected=true assertionUnchanged=true. Its embedded negative controls preserved currentGreenPasses=false for a simulated current regression and withheld the legacy selector when corrupted-relation rejection was false. verification_pin_guard_check returned allow with matched=true for the exact pinned selector and deny with matched=true for the proposed replacement selector.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/red/red-bfe8f-ledger-runtime-integrity.mjs:94-97,380-395 — CHK-001:edge:3 current-state regression coverage is not fail-closed. legacyPinnedNegativeControl eligibility omits currentGreenPasses, while simulatedCurrentRegression checks only the new currentGreenPasses token. A source-extracted mechanical probe of the committed renderer returned oldSelectorStillMatchesWhenCurrentGreenFails=true. Therefore the immutable old selector can still match a rendered currentGreenPasses=false state through nested compatibility text instead of requiring current GREEN success. Include currentGreenPasses in legacy-selector eligibility and add a negative assertion that the old selector is absent for the simulated current failure, while preserving the existing corrupted-relation-acceptance rejection control.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by proof-or-stop-implementer commit 025a128360382673e3edf74ecee51618bf16fd65. Independent test-coverage review run B-fe8f:RR-052 extracted the committed renderer and observed oldSelectorPresent=false for currentGreenPasses=false, oldSelectorPresent=false when corrupted-relation rejection was false, and oldSelectorPresent=true only for the current proven GREEN state. The complete RED/GREEN harness exited 0 with historicalBaselineFails=true currentGreenPasses=true currentCorruptedRelationRejected=true assertionUnchanged=true and gaps=0.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:902-923 does not validate the persisted outer requestDigest for a current signed ledger receipt. Independent current-build repro cloned the B-fe8f ledger, changed only receipts[index].requestDigest to 64 zeroes, and queryFindingLedger still returned accepted=true (original=bab7..., mutated=0000...). The query checks the signed receipt, operation, record IDs and exactRequestDigest, but never recomputes requestDigest from the committed carrier. The existing incomplete-tamper matrix at packages/main/src/tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:1643-1660 mutates other fields only. This violates CHK-005 and Section 9.3 stable read-only scorecard tamper refusal: an unsigned carrier identity field can be relabelled without rejection.

Legacy Finding terminal transitions are not crash-recoverable. packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:169-202 durably appends a legacy_identity_binding and assigns finding.recordId only in the in-memory compatibility mirror; lines 263-287 then durably append the signed lifecycle transition before the caller rewrites findings.json. If the process dies in that window, packages/main/src/core/store.ts:564-586 projects recordIds only from recordType=finding, not legacy_identity_binding, while lines 603-607 require candidate.recordId === transition.findingRecordId. An isolated current-build StoryStore repro deliberately omitted the post-transition mirror write and returned {durableTransitionRows:1,mirrorRecordId:null,projectedStatus:"open"}. Thus an acknowledged resolved/dismissed legacy Finding reappears open after crash, violating the Section 9.3 crash/retry and exactly-once lifecycle contract; add recovery projection for the signed legacy binding and a kill-window regression.
